abstract.p: Control system for an information/communications network, comprising a communications network (1), network-control means (2) and information-processing means (3). By means of quality-control means (4), a user (5, 6) may set the desired quality (UPS). In addition, the quality-control means measure the quality delivered by the information-processing means and compare the two. By reference to the calculated comparison result, parameters are passed on to the network-control means, in order to minimise the difference between the desired and delivered qualities. The quality-control means (4) may comprise one or more user agents which may be set by way of the information-processing means (3) and the communications network (1) by the user (5, 6).

Système de gestion d'un réseau d'informations/communications comprenant un réseau de communications (1), un moyen (2) de gestion du réseau et un moyen (3) de traitement d'informations. A l'aide d'un moyen (4) de contrôle de qualité, un utilisateur (5, 6) peut établir la qualité voulue (UQS). De plus, le moyen de contrôle de qualité mesure la qualité remise par le moyen de traitement d'informations et compare les deux. En référence au résultat de comparaison calculé, des paramètres sont transmis au moyen de gestion du réseau, afin de réduire au minimum la différence entre les qualités voulues et obtenues. Le moyen (4) de contrôle de qualité peut comprendre un ou plusieurs agents utilisateurs pouvant être établis à l'aide du moyen (3) de traitement d'informations et du réseau de communications (1) par l'utilisateur (5, 6).

description.p: Control system for an IC network.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

The invention relates to a control system for an information/ communications network, comprising a communications network, network-control means and information-processing means. Advanced telecommunications networks are bearer oriented.

A telecom operator does not know for which applications customers are using his communications network. In this case and in the description below, "applications" implies the whole of hardware (PCs etc.) and software (control and application software) which customers are using for, e.g.,
Internet browsing, e-mail, video meetings etc.

The customer has an opinion on the quality of the application making use of the bearer (the network) ,- not on the quality of the bearer itself. From the operator, however, it is expected that he provides sufficient Technical Quality of Service
(= TQS) to the customer.
The present invention relates to a system for determining the minimum required technical QoS (TQS) in the network (bearer) on the basis of the "User-perceived" QoS (UQS) desired by the customer.
Several mechanisms for providing TQS guarantees in a network are generally known. Frequently, guarantees are provided on TQS parameters, such as "bit error rate", "packet loss",

"throughput bit rate" and "delay" . In addition, various mechanisms are known for measuring UQS, e.g., for transmission chains comprising speech or video coders and decoders. The known systems, however, have the drawback that any coupling between the TQS guarantees (operator) and the UQS wishes (customer) is lacking.

Said coupling is hard to make and, in addition, depends on the terminal and the wishes of the customer. The customer eventually observes a quality which for the major part is determined by the terminal . If there are problems with said quality, the operator is often (unjustly) blamed. The customer just wants to get "value for his money" or, in other words, a maximum overall quality-price ratio.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The invention provides for a system, with which the quality desired by the user (UQS) may be set and maintained by measuring the quality delivered (UQS') as observed by the customer, and by comparing the two, UQS and UQS', with one another and by computing, from the comparison result, minimum TQS requirements for the network. Since here it concerns the settings effected by a user on the one hand, and the quality "experienced" by the user (to be measured by the system) , for the execution of all this there is preferably made use of one or more user agents, i.e., software modules which are capable, in several locations of the telecommunications network and information-processing systems associated therewith, "on behalf of the user", of observing and affecting specific processes. The user agent determines (computes) , on the basis of the set preferences of the customer and the characteristics of the application on the one hand, the optimum settings for the application (possibly including control hardware and software) and on the other hand the optimum TQS parameters for the network, so that the resulting UQS, UQS' ("1st Wert"), approximate the UQS, which is set by the customer as being desired ("Soil Wert"), as well as possible. Since the system measures the quality realised (UQS1) and the quality desired (UQS) , it will be able -provided the system is aware of the characteristic properties of the application- to determine the most efficient network settings (TQS) . The application characteristics are derived by the system -in this case the user agent- from the application. The user agents are set, from the information-processing systems, by setting software. Said setting software is preferably constructed as a plug-in of the application applied by the user, e.g., a plug-in of the videoconferencing software applied by the user.

Finally, it should be noted that, if the user agents may be provided with artificial-intelligence capabilities, as a result of which they need not accurately know in which way exactly the image, sound etc. presented to the users improve or deteriorate, but where the agents discover this in an iterative trial-and- error process and thus learn the setting rules for the application themselves.

By applying said invention, the operator may focus on the realisation of the TQS parameters requested by way of the user
agent, and is no longer held liable for unjust UQS requirements which are the result of the applications for which the user is responsible.
DESCRIPTION OF THE FIGURE

The operation of the invention is further explained by reference to the accompanying FIG. 1. FIG. 1 shows a comunications network 1 run by a network operator, controlled by a network-control server 2 (typically, large networks are controlled by a large number of control servers which are coupled to the network and to one another by way of a control or signalling network) .
To the network 1, there are connected application terminals

3 having users 5 and 6, respectively, who may enter into connection with one another in order to exchange -under the control of application modules activated within said terminals 3- with one another, e.g., for the benefit of an IP videoconferencing session. In this connection, the (technical) QoS, TQS is controlled by the control server 2. In this exemplary implementation, there is additionally connected, to the network

1, a UQS server 4. Said server co-operates with both the network server 2 and the user terminals 3, i.e., with the applications active thereon. It is proposed that all signals between the drawn components 2...4 be exchanged by way of the network l using, e.g., the Internet Protocol (= IP); by the way, other protocols are imaginable as well. On the UQS server 4, a user- agent platform (agent software) is active, comprising a user agent of each of the users 5 and 6. Each agent within the server

4 may be set by his or her user, as the case may be, by way of his/her terminal, with an agent-setting application active thereon, which may possibly be implemented as a subapplication -e.g., a plug-in- of the terminal application. By way of the network, the settings desired by the users 5 and 6 are thus passed on to their agents on the server 4, relating to, e.g., a video conference having, e.g., high-quality video images, including stereo hi-fi sound. Either initiated by the agents or by the terminal applications, the characteristic properties of said applications are passed on to the agents, as well as a number of variables which together serve as a measurement signal which is characteristic of the quality experienced by the users
of the, in this case, video and audio signals. There are known algorithms which, by way of mathematical processing of the video and audio signals received, provide such measurement signals. During the exchange of the video and audio signals -encoded into digital signals- during the video-conferencing session, there are therefore continuously transmitted UQS measurement and control signals between the user applications active on the terminals 3 and the UQS server 4. Said server 4 attempts to optimaise the UQS by, on the one hand, modifying -if so required- the settings of the applications active on the terminals 3 -whose characteristic properties server 4, after all, knows- and, on the other hand -once again, if required- by applying at the control server 2 -once again by way of the network 1- for modification in the TQS allotted. The latter may imply the application for a higher TQS -which is typically more expensive- or rather the application for a lower -cheaper- TQS, namely, if the UQS desired by the users may be attained by a lower TQS, but a better, optimum setting of the application parameters and possibly the parameters of the control system of the terminal 3 (e.g., screen settings, transmission rate, IP settings) .

Users will generally endeavour to minimise the communication costs . The user agents on server 4 will therefore always attempt, in the event of simultaneous optimisation of the setting of the parameters of the local applications, to make use of a minimum TQS, to be set by the network server 2 under control of the user agents within server 4. In addition, the agents may be instructed -by the users- that the TQS is not permitted to be higher than corresponds to a specific amount of money per time unit.

claim.claim-text: 1. Control system for an information/communications network, comprising a communications network (l) , network control means (2) and information-processing means (3) , characterised by quality-control means (4) for having a user (5, 6) set the desired quality (UQS) , for measuring the quality delivered by the information-processing means (UQS ' ) , and for comparing the desired and delivered qualities, and for computing, from the comparison result, and passing on, to the network-control means (2) , parameters for minimising the difference between said desired and delivered qualities.

2. Control system according to claim 1, characterised in that said quality-control means (4) comprise one or more user agents, i.e., software modules which may be set by the user (5, 6) by way of the information-processing means (3) and the communications network (1) , which user agents, by reference to the set preferences of the user and the characteristics of the information-processing means (3) , compute the optimum settings for the information-processing means and the optimum-quality parameters for the network so that the difference between the quality desired by the user (UQS) and the quality delivered to the user by the information-processing means is minimal, and said user agents pass said optimum settings on to the network-control means (2) .

3. Control system according to claim 2 , characterised in that the information-processing means (3) pass on parameters, algorithms and variables relating to the quality delivered to the users by the information-processing means, by way of the network (1) to the quality-control means (4) .

4. Control system according to claim 2, characterised in that the quality-control means (4) derive parameters, algorithms and variables relating to the quality delivered to the users by the information-processing means (3) iteratively from the behaviour and course of the values of the parameters and variables exchanged between the information-processing means (3) and quality-control means (4) .
5. Control system according to claim 2 , characterised in that the user agent may be set by a user by way of a module within the information-processing means (3) constructed as a plug-in.
